title: fix(doctor): avoid repeated state copies in full reports
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full shared-state database copies within a read-only Doctor report, which make diagnostics expensive on large installations.

Fixes #153067 (the read-only Doctor path). Related: #153276 and #153512.

## User Impact

Full Doctor reports reuse private state bytes for ordinary reads while preserving the live database and its WAL files. Each subsequent report reads a fresh snapshot. Selected checks remain on demand; independent verification and writable inspectors retain their copies. No configuration, schema, dependency, or CLI changes are required.

In the matched Linux fixture, seven reports wrote 7.03 GB to staging instead of 21.76 GB. Retaining the report snapshot increases sampled peak temporary occupancy from 184 MiB to 339 MiB for a 154 MiB database; all temporary files were removed afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary idle Gateway, status, and session-list reads produced no snapshot writes in this fixture. Doctor's artifact-preserving contract still requires private copies, but ordinary checks were preparing separate snapshots within the same report. The report now uses the existing retained snapshot lifecycle after update-budget admission and before state inspection. Completed update reports preserve their findings and exit code if private snapshot disposal fails; that disposal-only failure becomes a warning.

Reuse ends with the report; there is no completed-snapshot fingerprint cache. The contributor has since addressed the two initial race findings in their separate cache proposal. Thanks @MasterSwords1 for analyzing the snapshot cost and @dmlau76 for reporting it. This is an independent implementation.

The separate Windows catalog-consent workflow documented by the related PR is outside this Linux fixture; these results do not establish an issue-wide absence of catalog copying.

## Evidence

Two clean native Testbox source deliveries on the same lease, each with a 161,439,744-byte database, three configured agents, nine idle sessions, a 600-second window, 35 status commands, seven Doctor reports, and 96 session-list reads:

| Metric | Pinned main | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Doctor total staging-tree writes, including admitted-command tail | 21,760,540,857 B | 7,026,912,293 B |
| Full shared-state images per report | 19 | 6 |
| Idle / UI-only / status CLI staging writes | 0 | 0 |
| Gateway's one deferred verifier batch | 163,433,180 B | 163,433,180 B |
| Final staging directories / bytes | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

Doctor writes fell 67.7%. All commands, session-identity/idle assertions, readiness checks, tracing coverage, source-freshness checks, and managed-service cleanup passed. Session-list polling used the real RPC payload every five seconds; current UI refresh is event-driven. Byte counts are logical staging-tree writes, including private plugin captures, not physical-device throughput. No active-provider or forced-due-heartbeat claim is made.

- Real-WAL regressions fail before the fix, then prove within-report reuse, next-report freshness, unchanged source artifacts, and cleanup. Strict-disposal rejection tests preserve both healthy and blocking update outcomes.
- 81 read-only state tests, 25 Doctor isolation/cleanup tests, and 27 Doctor selection/budget/warning tests passed; the seven-case snapshot-admission suite also passed after the final getter simplification.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed. Fresh independent P1 review found no accepted actionable findings.
- The actual published `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater installed the packaged candidate successfully in `projects-doctor` with manual restart; candidate and installed payload identities matched.

Native Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35497634541. The wrapper commands returned exit 0; the linked hydration run can appear cancelled after owned lease cleanup. Main was pinned at `a0ec9f5c09d8009ab8c241027b806683881535b0`; candidate source hashes were verified before/after both observations and packaging. Earlier non-idle and development-rebuild captures were excluded.

The committed tree exactly matches the tested native candidate tree: `c981f8cec1d92e5993bd2e65dcc1511b343480c5`.

Production delta: +53/−13 (net +40); tests: +60/−22 (net +38); docs: +5.

## Review follow-up

ClawSweeper's sole before-merge request, **Add data-model compatibility proof**, is addressed by the published `openclaw@2026.9.4` updater-to-packaged-candidate installation recorded above. The install succeeded with matching candidate and installed payload identities. Source inspection confirms this patch changes only the lifetime of private read snapshots and disposal-error handling; it does not change a persisted schema, stored data format, migration, or backfill. A new migration fixture is therefore not applicable. The real-WAL regressions additionally cover unchanged source artifacts and fresh data in the next report. The review reported no correctness or security findings and listed no additional Rank-up moves.
